## Encoders and embeddings

Keyword search finds rows that share words with the query. Semantic
search finds rows that mean something close to it, even with no word in
common: “car” can find a passage about automobiles. It works by turning
each piece of text into an embedding, a fixed-length list of numbers (a
vector) placed so that texts with similar meanings sit close together.
The model that does this is the encoder. At indexing time the encoder
embeds every chunk and the vectors are stored; at query time it embeds
the query, and the search returns the chunks whose vectors are nearest.

A query and the documents it searches must be embedded by the same
encoder. Vectors from two different models live in unrelated spaces, so
comparing them gives meaningless distances without any error. This is
why a store records which encoder wrote it (see
[`encoder_id`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#encoder_id)
below).

litesearch’s default encoder is
[`static_embedder()`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#static_embedder),
which loads [model2vec](https://github.com/MinishLab/model2vec)’s
`potion-multilingual-128M`. A model2vec model is static: it holds one
precomputed vector per token and embeds a text by averaging the vectors
of its tokens. There is no neural network to run, so it needs no GPU and
no ONNX runtime, and it embedded about 8,600 chunks of 500 characters a
second on an Apple-silicon Mac. It returns 256-dimensional float32
vectors and covers many scripts, Devanagari included.
[`Index`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/api.html#index) uses
it unless you pass another encoder. `static_code_embedder()` loads
`potion-code-16M-v2`, a model2vec model trained on source code; nothing
in litesearch uses it by default, so pass it yourself if you index code.
Both functions cache the model per name, so every caller shares one
copy. The multilingual model is about 500 MB.

`evals/` found that the choice of encoder moves retrieval quality less
than chunk size or reranking do. Across four encoders the spread was
0.018 to 0.046 weighted MRR, and the static model won one of the three
test corpora outright.

When a transformer is worth the extra time,
[`FastEncode`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#fastencode)
runs one through ONNX Runtime. The dicts in the next cell name models
that have been tried with it; each gives the Hugging Face repository,
the ONNX file inside it and, where the model needs them, prompt
templates. You can pass any of these, any other model2vec model name to
[`static_embedder`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#static_embedder),
or your own object with an `.encode` method.

### FastEncode: transformer models through ONNX

[`FastEncode`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#fastencode)
runs a text embedding model exported to ONNX, a portable format for
neural networks, with ONNX Runtime. It works with most ONNX models that
ship a Hugging Face tokenizer. On first use it downloads the model with
[`download_model`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#download_model),
which reuses the local Hugging Face cache when the files are already
there. The default model is EmbeddingGemma 300M, which gives
768-dimensional vectors.

Each text is split into tokens, cut off at the smaller of the model’s
own limit and 512 tokens (`max_seq_len` replaces the 512), and run
through the model. The per-token outputs are averaged into one vector,
scaled to length 1 when `normalize=True`, and returned as float16 by
default. Texts are sent in batches of `batch_size`, `parallel` runs
batches on that many threads, and `stream=True` returns the batches one
by one instead of one joined array. `quantize='int8'` or `'uint8'`
writes a smaller quantized copy of the model beside the original on
first use and runs that instead.

Many embedding models are trained to see a short prefix that says
whether a text is a document or a query, such as `search_query:` for
nomic models. `encode_document` and `encode_query` add the prefix from
the model’s `prompt` templates; `encode` adds none.

FastEncode needs onnxruntime, which is not installed with litesearch
(`pip install onnxruntime`). If the model fails to download or load, the
constructor prints the error instead of raising, and every later
`encode` call prints a message and returns None. Check the result before
you store it. Qwen embedding models handle their padding token
differently and do not work with FastEncode yet.

### FastEncode

``` python
def FastEncode(
    model_dict:fastcore.basics.AttrDict={'model': 'onnx-community/embeddinggemma-300m-ONNX', 'onnx_path': 'onnx/model.onnx', 'prompt': {'document': 'title: none | text: {text}', 'query': 'task: search result | query: {text}'}}, # a model dict above: repo, ONNX file path and prompt templates
    repo_id:NoneType=None, # Hugging Face repo with an ONNX file, used instead of `model_dict`
    md:NoneType=None, # local folder holding the model files
    md_nm:NoneType=None, # path of the ONNX file inside the model folder
    normalize:bool=True, # scale each vector to length 1
    dtype:type=float16, # output dtype
    tti:bool=False, # pass token type ids to the model, as BERT-style models expect; also set by `model_dict.tti`
    prompt:NoneType=None, # dict with `document` and `query` templates containing `{text}`
    hf_token:NoneType=None, # Hugging Face token; defaults to the HF_TOKEN environment variable
    batch_size:int=32, # texts per ONNX call
    parallel:int=0, # threads that encode batches at once; 0 encodes in the calling thread
    quantize:NoneType=None, # run a quantized copy of the model: None, 'int8' or 'uint8'
    max_seq_len:NoneType=None, # token limit per text in place of 512; the model's own limit still applies (e.g. 64 for SigLIP2)
):
```

*A text encoder that runs a Hugging Face ONNX model with ONNX Runtime.*

assert _cached_snapshot('does-not/exist-xyz') is None           # missing repo -> None, never raises
print('download_model cache test passed:', p)

### doc_encoder

``` python

    embedder:FastEncode|StaticModel

```

*A function that embeds a list of documents with `embedder`, using its
document prompt when it has one.*

[`doc_encoder`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#doc_encoder)
and
[`query_encoder`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#query_encoder)
give every encoder the same shape: a function that takes a list of
strings and returns their vectors. For a
[`FastEncode`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#fastencode)
they call `encode_document` or `encode_query`, so the model’s prompts
are added. For anything else, a model2vec model or your own object, both
call `.encode` and the two functions behave the same.
[`Index`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/api.html#index) builds
both from the encoder you give it.

[`encoder_id`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#encoder_id)
names the model behind an encoder object, for example
`minishlab/potion-multilingual-128M`, with `+int8` appended for a
quantized
[`FastEncode`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#fastencode).
A string is returned as it is, and an encoder it cannot name gives `''`.
[`Index`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/api.html#index) passes
the name to `get_store(encoder=...)`, which records it with the store
the first time and raises
[`StoreMismatch`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/core.html#storemismatch)
if the store is later opened with a different one. Without that check,
adding vectors from a second model to an existing store would return
wrong neighbours with no error. An empty name never conflicts, so a
custom encoder with no name is not checked.

## Image encoding

[`FastEncodeImage`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#fastencodeimage)
embeds images the way
[`FastEncode`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#fastencode)
embeds text, so you can find pictures that look alike: store a vector
per image, embed a query image, and search. It takes Pillow images, file
paths or image bytes. Each image is converted to RGB, resized to a
square of the model’s input size (224 pixels by default) without
cropping, normalised with the model’s mean and standard deviation, and
run through the ONNX model. Where the model returns one output per image
patch, those are averaged into one vector. The default model is
nomic-embed-vision v1.5, with 768-dimensional float16 vectors.
`batch_size`, `parallel` and `stream` work as in
[`FastEncode`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#fastencode),
and the method is `embed` rather than `encode`. Like
[`FastEncode`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#fastencode),
it needs onnxruntime and returns None from `embed` when the model failed
to load.

## Text and images in one space

To search images with a text query, the text and image vectors have to
come from models trained together, so that a caption and its picture
land close to each other. There are two ways to get that here.

Some repositories ship a text model and an image model together, such as
SigLIP2.
[`FastEncodeMultimodal`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#fastencodemultimodal)
loads both from one repository and gives you `encode_text` and
`encode_image`. The default, `siglip2_so400m`, reads images at 512
pixels and cuts text at 64 tokens.

Other models come as a matched pair in separate repositories.
nomic-embed-text v1.5 and nomic-embed-vision v1.5 both produce
768-dimensional vectors in the same space, so load
`FastEncode(nomic_text_v15)` and `FastEncodeImage(nomic_vision_v15)`
separately and compare their vectors directly.

``` python
def FastEncodeMultimodal(
    model_dict:fastcore.basics.AttrDict={'model': 'onnx-community/siglip2-so400m-patch16-512-ONNX', 'vision_onnx': 'onnx/vision_model.onnx', 'text_onnx': 'onnx/text_model.onnx', 'img_size': 512, 'mean': [0.5, 0.5, 0.5], 'std': [0.5, 0.5, 0.5], 'max_seq_len': 64}, # a model dict with `vision_onnx` and `text_onnx` file paths
    normalize:bool=True, # scale each vector to length 1
    dtype:type=float16, # output dtype
    batch_size_text:int=32, # texts per ONNX call
    batch_size_image:int=16, # images per ONNX call
    parallel:int=0, # threads that encode batches at once; 0 encodes in the calling thread
    hf_token:NoneType=None, # Hugging Face token; defaults to the HF_TOKEN environment variable
):
```

*A text and image encoder pair loaded from one Hugging Face repo, such
as SigLIP2.*

``` python
from PIL import Image
import base64, io, os
from IPython.display import display
```

``` python
# Create 4 synthetic RGB images without needing any files
test_imgs = [Image.fromarray(np.random.randint(0, 255, (224, 224, 3), dtype=np.uint8)) for _ in range(4)]
img_enc = FastEncodeImage()  # default: nomic_vision_v15 (768-dim)

# Basic embed
embs = img_enc.embed(test_imgs)
assert embs.shape == (4, 768), f'Expected (4, 768), got {embs.shape}'
assert embs.dtype == np.float16
print(f'Basic image embed: shape={embs.shape}, dtype={embs.dtype}')

# Batching — batch_size=2 vs batch_size=4 must match
embs_b2 = img_enc.embed(test_imgs, batch_size=2)
embs_b4 = img_enc.embed(test_imgs, batch_size=4)
assert embs_b2.shape == embs_b4.shape == (4, 768)
assert np.allclose(embs_b2.astype(np.float32), embs_b4.astype(np.float32), atol=1e-3), 'image batching results mismatch'
print('Image batching test passed')

# Stream
stream_res = img_enc.embed(test_imgs, batch_size=2, stream=True)
assert hasattr(stream_res, '__iter__')
assert np.concatenate(list(stream_res)).shape == (4, 768)
print('Image stream test passed')

# Parallel
embs_par = img_enc.embed(test_imgs, batch_size=2, parallel=2)
assert np.allclose(embs_b2.astype(np.float32), embs_par.astype(np.float32), atol=1e-3), 'image parallel results mismatch'
print('Image parallel test passed')
```

    Basic image embed: shape=(4, 768), dtype=float16
    Image batching test passed
    Image stream test passed
    Image parallel test passed

``` python
# nomic paired — text (FastEncode) + vision (FastEncodeImage) share the same 768-dim space
nomic_enc     = FastEncode(nomic_text_v15, parallel=2)
nomic_img_enc = FastEncodeImage(nomic_vision_v15)

t_emb = nomic_enc.encode(['What does the Eiffel Tower look like?','What does the Eiffel Tower look like?','What does the Eiffel Tower look like?'])
i_emb = nomic_img_enc.embed([Image.fromarray(np.random.randint(0, 255, (224, 224, 3), dtype=np.uint8))])

assert t_emb.shape == (3, 768), f'Expected (3, 768), got {t_emb.shape}'
assert i_emb.shape == (1, 768), f'Expected (1, 768), got {i_emb.shape}'
assert t_emb.dtype == i_emb.dtype == np.float16
print(f'nomic paired: text={t_emb.shape}, image={i_emb.shape} — same space, ready for cross-modal search')
```

## Embedding a PDF without a store

[`encode_pdf_texts`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#encode_pdf_texts)
and
[`encode_pdf_images`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#encode_pdf_images)
embed a PDF and hand back plain tuples, leaving the table layout to you.
Use them when you keep vectors in your own schema instead of a
litesearch store.

[`encode_pdf_texts`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#encode_pdf_texts)
chunks the PDF with `pdf_chunks`, or with your own `chunk_fn`, embeds
the chunks with the encoder’s `encode_document`, and returns
`(page, chunk_idx, text, embedding)` for each, with pages counted
from 1.
[`encode_pdf_images`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#encode_pdf_images)
saves every PNG and JPEG image in the PDF to a temporary folder, embeds
them with an image encoder, and returns
`(page, image_bytes, embedding)`. Its pages are counted from 0, unlike
[`encode_pdf_texts`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#encode_pdf_texts).
Both return lists.

    Parallel test passed

``` python
# Semantic QA — modernbert should rank the transformer/attention passage highest
modern_enc = FastEncode(modernbert)
passages = [
    'The Transformer is a model architecture using self-attention mechanisms.',
    'Recurrent neural networks process sequences step by step.',
    'The model uses encoder and decoder stacks connected by attention.',
    'Convolutional networks excel at image recognition tasks.',
]
doc_embs = modern_enc.encode_document(passages).astype(np.float32)
query = 'What architecture replaces recurrence with self-attention?'
q_emb = modern_enc.encode_query([query]).astype(np.float32)
sims = (doc_embs @ q_emb.T).flatten()
best = int(sims.argmax())
assert sims[best] > 0.3, f'Expected similarity > 0.3, got {sims[best]:.3f}'
assert any(w in passages[best].lower() for w in ['attention', 'transformer', 'encoder'])
print(f'Semantic QA test passed: best match sim={sims[best]:.3f}')
print(f'Best: {passages[best]}')
```

    Semantic QA test passed: best match sim=0.527
    Best: The Transformer is a model architecture using self-attention mechanisms.

## Embedding with no model

[`hash_embed`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/utils.html#hash_embed)
makes vectors without any model or download, and gives the same vectors
on every run and every machine. It lowercases each text, takes every run
of 3 to 5 consecutive characters (character n-grams), hashes each run
with CRC32 into one of 256 slots, counts the hits per slot, and scales
the result to length 1. Two texts score high when they share many
character runs, so the vectors measure spelling, not meaning: “rank
fusion” is close to “rank fusions”, but “cat” and “feline” score near
zero.

It has two uses. One is matching names, such as people or places, where
shared spelling is most of the signal anyway. The other is an index
built where no real encoder can be downloaded, for example in a sandbox
without network access.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/Karthik777/litesearch/blob/main/litesearch/utils.py#L368"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### hash_embed

``` python
def hash_embed(
    texts, # strings to embed
    ndim:int=256, # length of each vector
    ngram:tuple=(3, 5), # shortest and longest character run to hash
    dtype:type=float16
):
```

*Unit-length vectors from hashed character n-grams, which match spelling
rather than meaning and need no model.*

``` python
from litesearch.utils import hash_embed
v = hash_embed(['rank fusion', 'rank fusion', 'a wholly unrelated sentence']).astype(np.float32)
assert v.shape == (3, 256)
assert (v[0] == v[1]).all()                 # same string, same vector
assert v[0] @ v[1] > v[0] @ v[2]            # and a shared spelling scores above an unshared one
assert abs(np.linalg.norm(v[0]) - 1) < 1e-2 # unit length, so a dot product is a cosine
```

``` python
# Devanagari is n-grammed as characters, so a codepoint is never cut in half
assert hash_embed(['सत्यमेव जयते', 'सत्यमेव जयते'])[0].tolist() == hash_embed(['सत्यमेव जयते'])[0].tolist()
```
